name: Kinematic twin and POH-referenced systems simulation

reference.handbook: Cessna Model 172N POH, 1 July 1978 — page-referenced values in data/poh_references.json
reference.authoritative_source: The aircraft-specific approved POH/AFM and supplements, Cessna/Lycoming maintenance and parts documentation

model.geometry_status: schematic; overall envelope from POH Figure 1-1; component locations from POH Section 7 text; not derived from drawings or an IPC

simulation.kinematics: js/kinematics.js — slider-crank pistons, firing order 1-3-2-4, valve events, spark timing
systems: gravity fuel system with selector and unusable fuel
28 V electrical with 60 A alternator, ACU over-voltage trip, low-voltage light
ISA pitot-static with pitot/static blockages and POH alternate-static calibration
simulation.physical_accuracy: illustrative; calibrated only to reproduce the POH figures listed in data/poh_references.json

tests.unit: npm test (node:test) — kinematics, POH-referenced simulation behaviour, scripted scenario completion
tests.browser: npm run test:e2e (Playwright Chromium) — load, engine start from the UI, piston motion, explode, part info, Arabic RTL, phone width
tests.model: npm run verify:model — rebuild and compare the GLB

phase6_corrections: Exploded view now works: every part node has its own pivot (Phase 6 GLB stored all vertices in world space with zero node translations)
Cylinder numbering follows Lycoming convention (odd = right bank, No.1 right-front); Phase 6 placed 1 and 2 on the same side
Single dual magneto per POH p.7-18 instead of two separate magnetos
Pistons are driven by crank angle (opposed pairs reach TDC together) instead of a sine offset
Phase 6 README listed C172N_Airframe_Approx.glb, which was not in the package; Phase 7 includes the airframe envelope in the same GLB
Viewer verified in a real browser (Phase 6 notes said it had not been)
safety: Educational approximation. Not for flight, maintenance, manufacturing or training credit.
